title: AnalysisResult
description: Shape of the JSON produced by `x64-disasm-cfg analyze --formats json` (single object) and by `x64-disasm-cfg batch` (a JSON array of these). Captured from a real backend run (src/report/mod.rs, src/analysis/*, src/stats/*, src/cfg/*, src/decoder/mod.rs) against corpus/tier1_straightline/pe_o0/insertion_sort.exe on the commit tagged in this repo's history. This file documents the contract both sides of the process boundary agree on; it is not consumed by either program at runtime. See docs/adr/0005-frontend-process-boundary.md.

accuracy.description: NOT CURRENTLY EMITTED. The type exists (src/report/mod.rs: `pub accuracy: Option<AccuracyReport>`, serde `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"`), but `pipeline::analyze` always passes `None` into `report::build`, so this key is always absent from real output today. The `batch` subcommand DOES compute mnemonic/length match percentages per binary (src/main.rs, via `analysis::oracle_accuracy::compare`), but only formats them into `summary.md`'s Markdown table — it never attaches an `AccuracyReport` back onto the per-binary object that becomes an entry in `summary.json`. The frontend works around this by parsing `summary.md`'s table (see `DisasmViewer/Services/BatchSummaryMarkdownParser.cs`) as a fallback data source. If the backend is later changed to populate this field, the frontend's `Models/AnalysisResult.cs` already has a matching `AccuracyReport` type ready to bind it directly, and `BatchSummaryMarkdownParser` can be retired in favor of it.

path.description: Exactly the string passed on the command line as <input>/<dir>. The frontend always resolves this to an absolute path before invoking the backend, so this field can be trusted as absolute and reused later (e.g. to regenerate DOT output for a batch-selected binary).

image_base.description: u64 on the Rust side; fits in a C# ulong.

FlowKind.description: Tagged union, serde `#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]`. `target` is present-but-possibly-null for cond_jump/jump/call (Option<u64> serializes as a null key, never an absent one), absent for sequential/return/terminate.

bytes.description: Lowercase hex, no separators, e.g. "55" or "4889e5".

operands.description: May be empty string (no serde skip — always present).

end.description: Exclusive: end_va of the last instruction in the block.

to.description: null means the synthetic exit node.

name.description: "sub_<hex entry>" unless the backend later resolves a real symbol name. Cross-reference against the binary's .symbols file client-side to classify user code vs CRT/runtime (see BatchSummaryMarkdownParser / symbol_filter.rs on the backend side) — this field alone does not carry that classification.

cyclomatic_complexity.description: i64 on the Rust side; E - N + 2.

indirect_resolved.description: Always 0 today — the decoder never resolves an indirect call/jmp target (see indirect_stats() in src/analysis/anti_disasm.rs).

return.description: Rust field is named `ret` internally, serde-renamed to "return" (a reserved word) on the wire.

complexity.description: One entry per function, sorted descending by cyclomatic_complexity.

AccuracyReport.description: See the top-level `accuracy` property note — this type is defined but never populated in current output.

x-batch-output-note.description: `x64-disasm-cfg batch <dir> --out <out>` writes <out>/summary.json as a bare JSON array of the AnalysisResult objects described above (one per binary found in <dir>), and <out>/summary.md as a human-readable Markdown table. IMPORTANT SCHEMA GAP: the Markdown table's 'Functions' and 'Max CC' columns show a user-code/total split (via symbol-file-based classification, src/analysis/symbol_filter.rs) and a 'Mnemonic %' / 'Length %' accuracy pair (via src/analysis/oracle_accuracy.rs) that are computed only for that Markdown string in src/main.rs — neither is attached back onto the AnalysisResult objects serialized into summary.json. Every entry in summary.json has the aggregate-only `stats.functions.count` / `stats.functions.max_complexity` (no user/total split) and `accuracy: null`. The frontend's Batch screen parses summary.md's table directly to recover these two numbers per binary (DisasmViewer/Services/BatchSummaryMarkdownParser.cs) since summary.json alone can't produce them without re-implementing the backend's symbol classification and oracle comparison client-side.
